papers.title: An amphibious untethered inchworm soft robot for fast crawling locomotion
papers.summary: Untethered soft robots are essential for advancing the real-world deployment of soft robotic systems in diverse and multitasking environments. Inspired by soft-bodied inchworm, we present a fully untethered soft robot with a curved, flexible structure actuated by magnetic forces. The robot has a total mass of 102.63 g and demonstrates multimodal locomotion, achieving a maximum walking speed of 3 . 7 4 c m / s and a swimming speed of 0 . 8 2 c m / s . papers.title: Compact Reinforcement Learning: Resource-Efficient Formulations for Large-Scale Decision Making
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a general framework for addressing problems involving sequential decision-making. However, modern practical applications of RL involve prohibitively large state and action sets: such as those in slate recommendations, image-based control, and large language-modeling tasks. Standard formulations of these problems demand intractable amounts of data and computational resources. papers.title: WAGRL: A Wind Adaptive Guidance Framework for Uncertainty-Aware UAV Trajectory Control
papers.summary: To address the challenges of wind-induced uncertainty, decision inconsistency, and safety risks in quadrotor trajectory tracking, this study presents a Wind Adaptive Guidance Reinforcement Learning (WAGRL) framework. Unlike conventional controllers relying on fixed aerodynamic models, WAGRL integrates ensemble-based policy learning with uncertainty-guided reinforcement learning to adaptively manage diverse wind conditions. papers.title: ASSIST AS NEEDED NANOROBOTIC NEUROREHABILITATION Motor-state estimation × minimum necessary assistance × transfer without assistance STARLI Research Works | Institute XXIII | Flagship 08 Author: Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Edition: Research Edition v1.0 | Nonclinical exploratory monograph PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION Can an adaptive rehabilitation device improve learning without quietly replacing the very human capability it aims to restore? This research edition investigates the distinction between successful machine-assisted task completion, independent motor capacity, and retained skill after assistance is withdrawn. The volume places assist-as-needed control inside a falsifiable scientific architecture. It considers latent fatigue and capability estimation, compliant actuation, feedback delay, voluntary effort, treatment-policy confounding, masked assistance withdrawal, cross-task transfer, fairness of comparisons, and reproducible nonclinical research. It evaluates whether complex adaptive strategies confer meaningful advantage over fixed-gain guidance, conventional rehabilitation robotics, dose-matched approaches, and carefully specified no-assistance controls. Its speculative micro- and nano-scale extension is intentionally bounded. The available references support motor learning and existing macroscopic robotic rehabilitation; they do not establish a safe or effective autonomous nanorobotic clinical intervention. No self-experimentation, human stimulation settings, invasive device instructions, or therapeutic claims are presented. RESEARCH CONTENT • Five-layer conceptual architecture: state estimation, minimum support, withdrawal, external transfer and successor reconstruction. • Thirty model derivation cards linked to individual chapters and Research Gates. • Eighty-two chapter-opening research theses and 410 separately paginated research sections. • Two hundred detailed Research Gates, each with a disprovable question, experimental sketch, competitor, stopping condition and follow-up route. • Twenty-four contextual DOI references with explicit distinctions between existing evidence and open hypotheses. • 111,011 machine-counted English words within the 410 chapter sections, plus 200 expanded Research Gates and mathematical prelude; phrase-level repetition remains substantial and independent originality certification is pending. The central principle is that the last scientific arbiter of rehabilitation is not how effectively a device moves, but what remains possible when the device no longer supplies the movement. Negative findings are treated as productive limits that can guide future investigators toward simpler, safer and more independently verifiable solutions.

papers.summary: Steel bridges are a critical component of the United States infrastructure, with more than 170,000 currently in service. Approximately 42% of these structures require urgent repair due to corrosion-related deterioration, which compromises the structural integrity of steel members and poses significant safety, economic, and societal risks. A common manifestation of this damage is severe section loss at beam-ends, often caused by leaking expansion joints that accelerate corrosion. papers.title: CNN-based multi-head attention with explainability via LIME for myocardial diagnosis in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
papers.summary: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is a non-invasive imaging modality widely used for assessing myocardial abnormalities, including inflammatory conditions such as myocarditis. However, the interpretation of CMR images is time-consuming and may be affected by inter-observer variability. In this study, we propose Ex-CMRNet, an explainable hybrid deep-learning framework for the automated detection of myocardial inflammation from CMR images.
